summary.headline: Fino Payments Bank's Q4 FY26 total revenue fell 31% YoY, while CASA base rose 22% to 1.75 crore accounts and renewal income hit a record ₹62.2 crore.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of heightened regulatory scrutiny, a deliberate risk-calibrated pullback in digital payments, and a mid-quarter governance event that led to interim leadership approved by RBI. Total revenue fell 31% YoY in Q4 and 14% for the full year, with the digital (UPI P2M) revenue dropping from ₹63 crore in Q3 to ₹41 crore in Q4. Retail deposits and CASA openings were the bright spot, with March 2026 showing 3.2 lakh new accounts and a record total deposit balance of ₹2,957 crore. Management is holding guidance back, has paused UPI P2M business pending a review, and is steering the bank toward SFB conversion with a stated 20% ROE target by FY30.

Approximately 6.9 lakh in Q4 FY26; 3.2 lakh in March 2026

financial_highlights.change: FY26 +25% YoY from ₹190 crore in FY25; Q4 is highest quarter ever

segments.name: Retail CASA and deposits
segments.commentary: CASA base reached 1.75 crore accounts (+22% YoY); March 2026 saw 3.2 lakh openings and record deposits of ₹2,957 crore. Cost of funds on core CASA book is below 2%.

segments.name: Renewal income
segments.commentary: Q4 renewal income of ₹62.2 crore was a record; FY26 renewal income rose 25% to ₹237 crore. CASA renewal run rate maintained at about 60-65%.

segments.name: Digital payments (UPI P2M / program manager)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell from ₹63 crore in Q3 to ₹41 crore in Q4 after derisking; active clients fell from 347 to 229. UPI P2M business is now paused, with existing merchants unable to transact and no new onboarding.

segments.name: Money transfer / B2B payments
segments.commentary: B2B digital payment throughput fell about 17% QoQ in Q4 after merchant-category and partnership exits. Management said DMT decline stemmed from the November 2024 RBI circular.

segments.name: Lending referral (SFB pilot)
segments.commentary: FY26 referral disbursals approximately ₹1,300 crore, with Q4 at ₹592 crore. Management said it earns about 100 bps on referrals and is not revenue-accretive currently.

segments.name: Business correspondence
segments.commentary: Revenue of approximately ₹140 crore in FY26. Not permitted under SFB; management said strategic options are being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given for FY27; management outlined four FY27 levers: CASA and liability growth, digital plan (to be announced toward end of the quarter), Aadhaar-enabled payment system upside, and CMS business recovery.

ROE target of 20% by FY30, supported by asset-light merchant-sourced model (about two-thirds of liabilities and assets) and cost of funds about 300 bps below a typical SFB (cost of funds about 3.9% in FY30).
Long-term SFB product mix about 90% secured: affordable housing, MSME, gold loans, LAP, micro LAP and some personal loans; NIM expected in a range of about 8-10%.
Technology capex of about ₹100 crore planned, primarily digital and technology infrastructure beyond core banking; branch expansion expected to be non-material.
SFB launch timelines stated as unchanged (Slide 22); RBI in-principle SFB approval granted 5 December 2025.
Reverse merger with promoter entity to be explored only if regulatorily allowed after SFB launch.
capex_capacity: Core banking system migration to Finacle completed in Q4 FY26 at about ₹200 crore investment; went live in January 2026 with 4-5 days of disruption.
Hollow-the-Core modular architecture developed to decouple high-frequency transaction handling from core, with the aim of reducing failure rates and supporting SFB scale.
Depreciation of ₹23 crore in Q4 FY26, driven by Finacle capitalisation; management said next year will carry a larger impact as this year reflects about 2.5 months.
Approximately 20 lakh physical merchants covering 98% of PIN codes; Soundbox deployed to a subset of these merchants (absolute number 2,951 cited).
Technology levers and specialised staff to be added for SFB preparation; a special review of the product and process in question is ongoing.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the revenue decline to regulatory-driven de-risking of digital payments from Q2 FY26, the industry-wide collapse of bank-led DMT remittances after the November 2024 RBI circular, and weakness in the NBFC and MFI sector affecting B2B.
Q4 CASA openings fell due to a 4-5 day disruption in January from the core banking migration and a deliberate focus on higher-balance customers.
UPI P2M business paused as of April 2026; management said April would have some residual revenue and then zero, with no new partner or merchant onboarding.
UPI incentive from Government of India received only until FY25; nothing received or factored into FY26 or FY27 per management.
Management declined to disclose April 2026 account-opening numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How will conflicts of interest with cash management and business correspondence be handled once the bank lends as an SFB?
qa_highlights.answer: CMS will continue as it is allowed under the payments model. BC business (around ₹140 crore revenue FY26) is not permitted under SFB and will be dealt with separately; strategic options are being looked at.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a capital raise planned for the SFB transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR is about 83% versus a 15% requirement and the business plan to FY30 (fee-based plus secured lending) does not need capital, so SFB launch is not dependent on a raise.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the Q4 CASA account-opening dip and will Q1 FY27 normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to the January core banking migration disruption (4-5 days) and a focus on higher-quality, higher-balance customers. Management expects the March momentum to continue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the procedure and timeline for the fit and proper assessment of Mr. Rishi Gupta?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board and RBI are evaluating the guidance; a special review of the product and process in contention is underway. No timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: How do you break down the 20% ROE target into yields, NIM and opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds about 3.9% in FY30 (about 300 bps advantage); NIM range of about 8-10% indicated; about 90% of the portfolio to be secured. Detailed yield and opex breakdown deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How much of CASA revenue is float income?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about ₹630 crore CASA revenue in FY26, ₹136 crore is float revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% ROE target for FY30 or earlier, and does the ₹100 crore investment include branch costs?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE of 20% targeted by FY30. The ₹100 crore capex is primarily technology infrastructure; branch costs are expected to be non-material given the merchant-led model.

risks_watch: Digital payments revenue and throughput: UPI P2M paused with no timeline; April revenue expected near zero; revised digital plan due toward end of Q1 FY27.
Governance: Rishi Gupta unavailability and fit-and-proper review pending with Board and RBI; special review ongoing; interim CEO and CFO in place.
SFB conversion conditions (network, capital adequacy, promoter shareholding, branch rollout, differentiated business plan) under RBI framework; promoter holding is about 75%.
Depreciation step-up and interest cost increase from reverse repo participation weighing on PBT and PAT; management said EBITDA impact was only ₹6-7 crore.
Account-opening momentum after the Q4 disruption; April 2026 numbers not disclosed.
Reverse merger and BC business sale status unresolved; no quantified guidance for FY27 profitability.
summary.management_tone: Confident on deposits, renewal income and SFB timelines, but evasive on specifics: it declined FY27 guidance, April account numbers, the digital plan and the fit-and-proper timeline, deferring them to later updates.

Our renewal income in Quarter 4'26 reached ₹62.2 crores, the highest single quarter renewal in the bank's history.
So we are getting skewed towards the CASA liability. That is our strength.

adds.what: Finacle core banking system migration (capitalised, went live Jan 2026) - not new productive capacity
Technology infrastructure capex of about ₹100 crore (digital and tech infrastructure, not productive capacity)

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance; management cites four levers (CASA growth, digital plan TBA, Aadhaar-enabled payments, CMS recovery) and a 20% ROE target by FY30 with SFB conversion, but digital P2M is paused, Q4 revenue fell 31% YoY, and backing is largely aspirational.

mgmt.note: Management discussed a mid-quarter governance event that led to interim leadership approved by RBI; no specific new leader's growth plan was detailed in the brief.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27 onward, tied to SFB conversion
rows.why: Margins rose +250 bps QoQ and +500 bps on a full-year basis, but no absolute margin figure was given, FY27 guidance was withheld, and digital P2M revenue fell from ₹63 crore in Q3 to ₹41 crore in Q4 with UPI P2M now paused.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Finacle migration (₹200 crore) is already commissioned and branch expansion is described as non-material, so no new productive capacity is in the window; the ₹100 crore technology capex is infrastructure, not capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: CASA base rose 22% YoY to 1.75 crore and March 2026 added 3.2 lakh accounts, but B2B throughput fell ~17% QoQ, active digital clients fell from 347 to 229, and April 2026 account numbers were not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A ~₹100 crore technology capex is already planned for FY27, but there is no utilisation metric in the brief and the bank is capital-light (CRAR ~83% vs 15% requirement, no raise needed).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance, Q4 total revenue fell 31% YoY and FY26 fell 14%, and the digital plan is deferred to end of Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: UPI P2M revenue goes to near zero from April 2026 (₹41 crore in Q4 vs ₹63 crore in Q3), BC business (~₹140 crore FY26) is under strategic review, and depreciation steps up in FY27 after Finacle capitalisation (₹23 crore in Q4).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY27 digital plan, SFB product set over FY27-FY30
rows.why: A revised digital plan is to be announced toward end of Q1 FY27 and SFB product mix (~90% secured: housing, MSME, gold, LAP) is planned, but no launch dates were given.

rows.label: SFB conversion and 20% ROE by FY30
rows.why: RBI in-principle SFB approval was granted 5 Dec 2025 with timelines unchanged, CRAR is ~83% vs 15% requirement so no raise is needed, and the target is 20% ROE by FY30 with cost of funds ~3.9% (about 300 bps below a typical SFB); conversion conditions remain under RBI framework.

rows.label: Governance review: fit-and-proper assessment of Rishi Gupta
rows.why: Board and RBI are evaluating, interim CEO and CFO are in place, and management declined to give a timeline, so a leadership or regulatory outcome could still move the story.

rows.label: Renewal income and CASA momentum
rows.why: Renewal income hit a record ₹62.2 crore in Q4 (FY26 ₹237 crore, +25% YoY) with a 60-65% run rate, and management expects March's account-opening momentum to continue into FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on deposits, renewal income and SFB timelines, but declined FY27 numerical guidance, April account numbers, the digital plan and the fit-and-proper timeline; analysts pushed on the BC business, the ROE bridge and float income.
